main_body: A 32px-wide, 32px-tall sci-fi wall face made of blue-grey metal panels with an orange stripe near the top, recessed panels, a vent grille and a lower rail/skirting. It is a flat wall surface tile.
top_band: none; the wall is a vertical face. The top rows 0-2 are a light blue-grey cap line, not a horizontal surface.
evidence: The tile is a wall face (terrain kind), drawn as a flat front elevation. There is no top surface, only a 1-2px cap line at the top. Panels are inset with dark edges, but the overall piece is a vertical face. Because the kind is terrain, a wall face is a plausible match, but under the strict 3/4 contract there is no top band, so it fails.

style.evidence: The candidate has a coherent blue-grey ramp (light edge, mid, dark, deep) with tinted dark outlines rather than black, plus orange accents, rivets and a vent. It has less texture than the references, though: the large panel areas (around 8x10 px) are flat mid-blue with only a few dash highlights, with no grain or speckle. The references have per-stone and per-plank shading and many more colours per tile. This reads thinner and flatter than the Beodeul references.
